headline: GOLD ERASES ALL 2026 GAINS AS FED HIKE BETS SURGE TO 70% — Silver Dives 3.2% To $64.83; Bond Yields Hit 2008 High
snippet: Gold fell to $4,374 — effectively wiping out all of its 2026 year-to-date gains — as Friday's blowout August payrolls drove Federal Reserve rate-hike probability to 70% and sent global bond yields to their highest since 2008. Silver dropped 3.2% to $64.83 before steadying. Fed Governor Michael Barr warned the central bank must stay prepared to hike if inflation persists, reinforcing the hawkish tone from Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole speech. The September 15–16 FOMC meeting is now firmly a live hike decision.

headline: MIATA METALS HITS 96m AT 1.41 g/t AT SELA CREEK — Best-Ever Intercept, New 3km Discovery Zone Confirmed; CSE: MMET +11%
snippet: Miata Metals (CSE: MMET / OTCQX: MMETF) reported its best-ever drill intercept at the Sela Creek Gold Project in Suriname — 96 metres at 1.41 g/t Au at the Big Berg target — while also confirming a new Puma East discovery 3km southeast of the main Jons Trend–Big Berg corridor. Two rigs remain active across the 25,000m 2026 campaign with ~10,300m drilled and several assays pending. Shares jumped 11%.

headline: VALE SHELVES VBM IPO AMID BRAZIL PUSHBACK — Cu-Ni-Co Portfolio Worth Billions Stays Private; Future Listing Preserved
snippet: Vale has indefinitely shelved the planned IPO of Vale Base Metals (VBM) — its copper, nickel and cobalt subsidiary — after Brazil's government objected to ceding strategic influence over critical mineral assets. London-based VBM, carved out in 2023 for an eventual listing, holds Vale's battery-metals portfolio across Canada, Brazil, Japan, the UK and Indonesia. CEO Shaun Usmar had targeted mid-2026 readiness. A future listing remains possible but timing is now open-ended.

headline: ZAMBIA PLANS $1.8B GOLD FORMALISATION PUSH — ZCCM-IH Eyes Ghana Model To Capture Illicit Small-Scale Output
snippet: Zambia's state mining investor ZCCM-IH is targeting more than $1.8 billion in additional gold export revenue by formalizing its artisanal and small-scale mining sector, following the model Ghana used to establish its state gold board. The UAE officially imported nearly $1.8B of Zambian gold in 2023 while Zambia declared less than $128M in exports — a gap ZCCM-IH CEO Kakenenwa Muyangwa says formalisation will close. Ghana's ASM sector now outproduces its major mining companies, earning $10.8B in foreign currency.

headline: COPPER SLIDES TO 1-MONTH LOW AT $6.40 — Rising Oil, Global Yield Surge And US-Iran Tensions Knock Base Metals
snippet: Copper retreated toward $6.40/lb — its weakest level in a month — as surging global bond yields, rising oil prices and renewed U.S.-Iran hostilities weighed on commodities broadly. The pullback follows the 10-week winning streak that peaked at $6.60/lb. Comex inventories remain near record highs from tariff-driven front-loading while LME stocks outside the U.S. continue to tighten — a bifurcated market analysts say supports a medium-term recovery once macro headwinds fade.

headline: STANMORE BUYS MORANBAH SOUTH MET COAL FROM EXXARO FOR $105M — 743M-Tonne Queensland Resource Expands Bowen Basin Empire; ASX: SMR
snippet: Stanmore Resources (ASX: SMR) agreed to buy Exxaro Resources' Moranbah South metallurgical coal tenements in Queensland's Bowen Basin for US$105 million. The tenements hold 743 million tonnes of coal resources including 505Mt of hard coking coal, adjacent to Stanmore's Isaac Plains Complex. Completion is conditional on Exxaro first acquiring Anglo American's remaining 50% JV stake — a transaction expected to close before end of Q4 2026.

headline: SURGE BATTERY METALS MOBILIZES NEVADA NORTH BFS DRILL — September 2026 Start; 10.51 Mt LCE Resource; TSXV: NILI
snippet: Surge Battery Metals (TSXV: NILI / OTCQX: NILIF) and joint venture partner Evolution Mining have finalized the 2026 drill program at the Nevada North Lithium Project, with contractor mobilization targeted for September 2026. The campaign is designed to support a Bankable Feasibility Study through condemnation, pit-definition, geotechnical and hydrogeological drilling. The project's updated resource stands at 10.51 Mt LCE at 3,007 ppm Li — one of the larger undeveloped lithium deposits in the western U.S.

headline: SLAM EXPLORATION HITS 1.19% CuEq AT GOODWIN — New Sulphide Zone 2km From Known Deposits; New Brunswick; TSXV: SXL
snippet: SLAM Exploration (TSXV: SXL) reported 1.19% copper equivalent over 24.6 metres from the massive sulphide zone at its Goodwin Cu-Ni-Co project in New Brunswick's Bathurst Mining Camp. Hole GW26-36 confirmed a new sulphide discovery 2,000m northwest of the Logan zone, materially expanding the mineralized footprint at one of Canada's most underexplored VMS corridors. The 2026 program is ~37% complete, backed by a Province of New Brunswick drilling grant.

headline: VERMEULEN: GOLD MINERS JUST HAD THEIR BEST AUGUST IN 30 YEARS — But September's 70% Rate-Hike Bet Could Undo It Fast
snippet: Gold miners (GDX) posted their best August since 1994, surging 33% on record producer margins — more than triple bullion's advance. But technical analyst Chris Vermeulen warns September's 70% probability Fed rate hike is the critical variable. Long-term trends for gold remain bullish, short-term momentum is recovering from oversold post-NFP levels, and any FOMC-driven dip into the $4,300–$4,350 zone is more likely a buying opportunity than a structural reversal.

headline: MP MATERIALS SHIPS FIRST TEXAS MAGNETS — Pentagon Inks 10-Year NdFeB Deal At $110/Kg As US Mine-To-Magnet Chain Closes
snippet: MP Materials (NYSE: MP) has begun commercial sales of NdFeB permanent magnets from its Independence facility in Fort Worth, Texas — completing a U.S. mine-to-magnet rare earth supply chain the Pentagon has been funding since 2022. A 10-year DoD contract locks in 7,000 MT/year of magnet purchases at a $110/kg price floor, guaranteeing long-term offtake. A planned 10X Facility will expand total magnet capacity to 10,000 MT/year by 2028, directly challenging Chinese magnet market dominance.

headline: FOMC DECISION WEEK INCOMING — PPI, CPI, ADP And Michigan Sentiment All Print Before September 15-16 Fed Meeting
snippet: The week of September 7 delivers the densest macro calendar before the Federal Reserve's September 15–16 FOMC meeting: ADP employment (Wednesday), August PPI (Thursday), August CPI (Friday), and the University of Michigan preliminary September consumer sentiment. With rate-hike probability at 66–70%, any softer inflation print could sharply reverse gold's post-NFP selloff — while a hot CPI could send the dollar through resistance and push metals to new 2026 lows. Gold's consolidation range is $4,313–$4,645.
